_comment: Musical scene per artist, used to stop higher/lower pairing a track someone knows against one they have never heard of. 39% of pairs used to cross scenes, which is a coin flip rather than a judgement, and it was unplayable in both directions: a Spanish speaker got Arctic Monkeys against Bad Bunny. Runs now stay within one scene. Resolution order: artistScenes wins, then the first genre in genreScenes, then 'anglo'. The scene 'excluded' means never use the artist at all. Genres are matched exactly, never by substring: an earlier regex filed Ed Sheeran as k-pop because his tag 'folk-pop' contains 'k-pop'. Every key here must match a tag that really appears in data/artist-snapshot.json, checked by scripts/check-scenes.mjs, because an exact-match map fails silently: the first version of this file spelled the French tags 'rap francais' and 'variete francaise' without accents, so none of them ever matched and the entire french scene was dead, leaving Jul and Ninho sitting in anglo.

_allowUnmapped.afro house: Electronic subgenre used by DJs from anywhere, not the West African pop scene.
_allowUnmapped.afro-cuban jazz: Jazz lineage tag, not a language scene.
_allowUnmapped.latin afrobeats: Crossover tag, carried by anglo-market artists as often as not.
_allowUnmapped.swedish pop: ABBA and Zara Larsson record in English.
_allowUnmapped.batak: Carried by December Avenue, who are already routed to filipino by opm.

_notes.mneskin: Italian, records in both languages. Own scene rather than anglo.
_notes.selena-gomez--the-scene: Her former band, a separate Spotify artist from Selena Gomez. Two tracks, reads as a duplicate entry in a game.
_notes.pitbull: Heavy Latin crossover but the catalogue is anglo-market. Reviewed and kept.
_notes.camila-cabello: Same call as Pitbull. Reviewed and kept.
_notes.niki: Indonesian-born, but the catalogue is English-language 88rising output. Same call as Joji, who is the same case.
_notes.alok: Brazilian DJ whose big tracks are English-language dance records. Kept anglo on the same catalogue test.
_notes.rammstein: NOT overridden, so currently anglo, and this one is arguable. The catalogue is German-language, but the audience and playlisting are anglo-market rock. Move to german if runs start feeling off.
_notes.shakira: Left as latin on genre evidence, though Hips Don't Lie and Waka Waka are global anglo-market hits. Flip here if the pool feels thin.
_notes.no-genre-artists: 89 artists in this pool have no Spotify genre tags and fall through to anglo. The top of that list is Taylor Swift, The Weeknd, Billie Eilish, Coldplay, so the default is usually right, but it is a default rather than evidence.
_notes.unmapped-on-purpose: 'afro house', 'afro tech', 'afro-cuban jazz' and 'latin afrobeats' are electronic and jazz subgenres used by artists from anywhere, so they stay unmapped. 'swedish pop' likewise: ABBA and Zara Larsson record in English. 'classical' is too generic to route anywhere.
_notes.cline-dion: Carries the tag 'variété française', but the streamed catalogue is My Heart Will Go On and the other anglophone hits. Overridden rather than left to the genre map. Slug is 'cline-dion' because the slugifier strips accented characters rather than transliterating them, which is a separate pre-existing quirk affecting her public URL.
